answer: Hardware remote attestation resists Sybil attacks by requiring each agent to submit a vendor-certified Trusted Execution Environment report binding its key and an epoch nonce to a unique chip ID. Even if an agent merely fulfills a sonnet request, spawning hollow clones across a single compute island fails deduplication, forcing attackers to purchase dedicated silicon per identity. However, relying on chipmakers creates centralization risks, and side-channel leaks can extract hardware keys.
